notes: URDU CLIP ORDER for Coach.spokenMove(move,state,'ur'): normal move = [frag.piece.X, frag.sq.TO, frag.to] reads 'نائٹ ای فور پر'. Capture = [frag.piece.X, frag.sq.TO, frag.takes] reads 'نائٹ ای فائیو کیپچر' (optionally [frag.piece.X, frag.sq.FROM, frag.from, frag.sq.TO, frag.takes] 'نائٹ جی ون سے ای فائیو کیپچر'). Disambiguation/from: [frag.sq.FROM, frag.from, frag.sq.TO, frag.to] reads 'ای ٹو سے ای فور پر'. Castling = [frag.castle_short|frag.castle_long]. Promotion = [frag.sq.TO, frag.promote_to, frag.piece.X] reads 'ای ایٹ پروموشن کوئین'. Append frag.check_word or frag.mate_word at the end ('... چیک' / '... چیک میٹ'). Piece-hint (hint.tier2): line clip then [frag.piece.X]. English order is standard: [frag.piece.X, frag.to, frag.sq.TO] 'knight to e four'; capture [frag.piece.X, frag.takes, frag.sq.TO]; promotion [frag.sq.TO, frag.promote_to, frag.piece.X]; frag.on/frag.from are available for English ('on e four', 'from e two'). frag.on in Urdu is also 'پر'. Captions: ur uses Latin chess terms; say_ur is Urdu script only; placeholders never appear in say_*. Urdu text is gender-neutral by design (no first-person gendered verbs).
